To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated a highly purified enzyme from Xenopus ovary, a casein kinase of the type II, and that this enzyme has a biological role in the control of the meiotic cell cycle of Xenopus full-gown oocytes.
the Xenopus laeavis casein kinase II is a key regulator of meiotic cell cycle in Xenopus oocytes.

(i) a Xenopus lae-vis ovary casein kinase of the type II was purified and characterized; (ii) the kinase has been microinjected into Xenopus lae- vis oocytes to investigate its biological effects on the cell division; (iii) the enzyme inhibits progesterone-induced meiotic cell division; (iv) it facilitates maturation-promoting-factor-induced maturation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification, characterization and biological activity of a casein kinase II-like enzyme purified from Xenopus ovary.
a protein kinase that may have a role in the control of the meiotic cell cycle in Xenopus lae-vis.
the identification of the kinase targets in the meiotic cell cycle and with the elucidation of the mechanism by which the kinase regulates the meiotic maturation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinase could play a role in the regulation of the maturation-promoting-factor activity.
casein kinase II could be implicated in a regulatory mechanism of the cell division cycle, both in the meiotic and the mitotic cycles.
the enzyme is an important component in the meiotic cell cycle of Xenopus lae-vis oocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the casein kinase II is a multifunctional enzyme involved in the control of the cell division cycle.
the kinase could play a dual role in the meiotic cell cycle: a negative one during the prophase arrest and a positive one during the metaphase transition.

the kinase could be involved in the regulation of the meiotic cell cycle at different levels: (a) by inhibiting the meiotic probase arrest, (b) by facilitating the metaphase/anaphase transition, (c) by regulating the maturation promoting factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
casein kinase II is a key player of the oocyte meiotic cell division.
casein kinase II is a major player in the control of meiotic cell cycle progression in Xenopus lae vis oocytes.
the Xenopus casein kinase II is a multifaceted molecule which is able to exert its action at several levels of the meiotic maturation process.
